# the contributor audit of the R4 strict-count-quota profile certificate

Source: `candidate b78a2eb10bd3783f`.

UPDATE: Global attainment has since been proved and root audited in
`historical context (not an accepted premise)`. Conditional wording below
records the narrower scope of this original profile audit.

The complete integer base is defined by the three actual triangle
inequalities. Its31 points have parity sizes10,7,7,7. The strict full,
empty, and canonical-partial cap traces give12 full and3 partial fibers
per cap, hence Q=(40/3)V. The zero-slice base centroids sum to0, so the
displayed common section centroids and response weights are genuine
stationary data. They do not certify global cap minimization.

The analytic quota proof is correct. A complete one-parity trace has
at most one point. Every complete two-dimensional trace contains a
determinant-one triangle by the minimal-area argument using an integer
point in the edge parallelogram; hence a two-parity trace is collinear
and has at most9 points in the coordinate box. A three-parity trace
has at most21 points if it misses the even class. Otherwise it has at
most24 before closure is used; closure forces at least one of the three
even outer vertices to be absent, giving23. Proper four-parity traces
have at most30. These give the uniform strict margin1/124.

On each continuous facet, the three equal parameter intervals produce
exactly27 high and66 low points in the three-coordinate(z1,z2,s) list.
the contributor reran the standalone Fraction-only checker:732 exact checks PASS.
I also independently checked that the certificate has144 positive
edges and denominator least common multiple4,418,652, as stated.
The exact source masses22, target masses9 and coordinate barycenters
give Jensen's inequality for EVERY convex test after the common affine
map s->(r+s)/3. Integration in r gives precisely the coefficient40/93.
The finite certificate, not numerical feasibility of the exploratory
linear program, supplies this step. Constant tests attain equality.

The facet reduction is valid. For clarity, the base permutation maps
fix0 and send the underlying primitive vertices(-1,-1),e1,e2 to each
other; equivalently divide the D4 vertices by4. Thus their matrices
and inverses have integer entries. This is the precise unimodularity
reason; the scaled D4 vertices themselves are not an integer basis.
The continuous facet parameterization is affine and changes length by
one constant per facet. The argument therefore covers normal-dependent
potentials and arbitrary triangle shapes without a measure mismatch.

The edge supremum2/5 follows from the two paired convexity inequalities
at the central one of five equally spaced points. The corrected R3
comparison properly retains its zero-offset partial traces.

Independent finite base and continuous vertex permutations preserve
the actual measure and ambient halfspaces. Their orbit average is the
single feasible point(0,g). Convexity of raw depth superlevels makes
it a true global deepest point, regardless of its unknown numerical
depth. This does not prove its depth is Q. The all-normal inequality
in Section6 must still be established or refuted by an exact cap.

Even if that inequality holds, this example has depth far above the
OC target1/9. It would only refute an auxiliary individual-Gamma claim
under strict count quotas, not OC or a claim retaining bad normalized
depth and all attained-minimum hypotheses.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
